Product design document · August 2026

Shapes Agents

A mixed-reality application in the ShapesXR platform, built for XREAL AURA. People open an agent, speak naturally, and receive voice and spatial responses in the room around them.

Product familyShapesXR
ApplicationShapes Agents
DeviceXREAL AURA
ReleaseSigned APK · Google Play

01 · Product summary

Product definition

Shapes Agents is part of the ShapesXR platform, built as its own application for XREAL AURA. It is launched from ShapesXR and runs as a separate app; from there the user talks, and there is nothing to type.

01

Agent selection

Open an agent from the gallery and start talking. Sample agents are included with the application.

02

Voice interaction

The agent listens and answers aloud. A visible chat window doesn’t appear during normal use.

03

Spatial responses

The agent can add labels, arrows, panels, timers, zones, and 3D previews beside real objects.

02 · Entry from ShapesXR

Opening Shapes Agents

You can launch Shapes Agents from the ShapesXR lobby. See the picture below.

From ShapesXR

Launching the application

An Open Shapes Agents action sits in the ShapesXR header. Selecting it opens Shapes Agents and the user lands in the agent gallery. If it isn’t installed yet, the action takes them to Google Play first.

03 · Agent gallery

Choosing an agent

The gallery lists the available agents as cards. Selecting a card opens that agent. A separate action lets the user create an agent of their own.

Included

Sample agents

The application ships with a set of sample agents covering familiar physical tasks. Selecting a card opens the agent straight away.

Personal

Your agents

Agents the user has made appear alongside the samples, ready to open the same way.

Environment

Any room

Agents run in whatever space the user is standing in. No prepared or pre-scanned environment is required.

04 · Agent session

Agent session

Opening an agent replaces the gallery with the mixed-reality session. The application shows only the controls and spatial elements needed for the current task.

01

Open

The agent loads and the gallery clears from view.

02

Talk

The user speaks normally; a small status indicator shows listening, speaking, muted, or offline.

03

Respond

The agent answers aloud and places only the spatial UI needed for that response.

04

Session continuation and exit

The user can keep talking, ask to clear an item, or return to the gallery.

Secondary control

Return to the gallery

The user can say “go home” or “back to the gallery.” A control attached to the session panel provides the same action when voice isn’t practical, following the Android XR pattern for persistent navigation.

05 · Spatial UI

Spatial UI element library

Each item below has one clear role and one placement rule. The first ten are in scope for the MVP; the last three are stretch goals.

01

Arrow

Points to the next object, location, or direction of movement.

Placement
Floats close to the target without covering it.

02

Callout

Connects a short instruction to one precise part of an object.

Placement
The panel sits in open space; a leader line touches the target.

03

Circle marker

Marks a small object or area without adding text.

Placement
Conforms to the object or the surface beneath it.

04

Placement frame

Shows a square or rectangular area where something belongs.

Placement
Matches the edges of the shelf, surface, or open space.

05

Plain text label

Names an object or shows a short value with no panel behind it.

Placement
Sits beside the object when the background stays readable.

06

Backplate label

Keeps a short label readable against a busy or changing background.

Placement
Faces the user and stays close to the related object.

07

Spatial timer

Shows a live countdown for the current task.

Placement
Stays beside the appliance, object, or work area it controls.

08

Text panel

Presents an instruction, warning, short list, or summary.

Placement
Floats in a clear reading area near the task.

09

Image panel

Shows a diagram, reference photo, part view, or expected result.

Placement
Appears beside the object or step that needs the reference.

10

Text and image panel

Pairs one visual reference with one short instruction.

Placement
Faces the user and stays near the active work area.

11Stretch Goal

Step and progress panel

Shows the current step and how much of the task remains.

Placement
Stays near the task station without following the center of view.

12Stretch Goal

Path and zone

Marks a walking route, work boundary, or drop-off area.

Placement
Sits directly on the floor or another detected surface.

13Stretch Goal

3D object preview

Previews an object, part, pose, or arrangement at useful scale.

Placement
Rests on a surface or appears beside the physical item it explains.

06 · Example agents

Example agents

Sample agents introduce the product through familiar physical tasks. Each runs in whatever room the user is standing in, with no prepared environment.

01

Kitchen Helper

Guides a recipe using the ingredients and appliances already in view.

Labels, arrows, timers, step panels

02

Repairs Assistant

Guides a repair step by step and identifies the part in question.

Callouts, circle markers, image panels

03

Interior Designer

Suggests where furniture could go and previews arrangements in the room.

3D object preview, placement frames, text and image panels

04

Warehouse Sorter

Directs a picker to the right shelf and marks the drop-off area.

Path and zone, placement frames, labels

07 · MVP definition

MVP scope

The MVP is ready when a new user can open Shapes Agents from ShapesXR, choose an agent, speak to it, and receive clear spoken and spatial responses in their own space.

Included

  • Agent gallery with a set of sample agents
  • Voice-led sessions using the defined spatial UI set
  • Voice creation of new agents
  • Signed APK for XREAL AURA with Google Play distribution

Product boundaries

  • The application doesn’t show a persistent chat window during a session
  • The first release uses the defined spatial UI set
  • Returning to the gallery is a secondary control rather than a primary feature
  • Agents run in unprepared real-world spaces; no environments ship with the application
